I love when old computer shit gets posted in here.

What can I say about these things.. Zip disks and drives certainly had their time in the sun for a very brief period in the mid to late 90's. They bridged the gap between the 1.44 Mb floppy disk that preceded it and the CD-R/RW that came out not too much long after (Zip was introduced in 1994, I started burning CD's in 1998). Also, Flash and USB flash storage was in it's infancy at the time.. this plus the popularity of CD-R eventually helped propel the Zip technology into obsolescence.

Although the Zip disk was very convenient as opposed to the long burn times and fragile nature of CD-R, the technology suffered because the media was expensive compared to CD-R discs, CD-R was compatible with most CD Players and burning music was extremely popular so people always had them around, and the Zip drives themselves suffered from serious quality issues (click, click, click, of death) for a time. CD-RW technology was available at the time, these could be erased and re-used just like a Zip disk, but I can't remember a single person back then who ever used them. Everyone just had a stack of CD-R's, used them once, and tossed them because they were so dang cheap.

Iomega also released a removable media disk-type device called the Jaz drive that looked very similar to a Zip drive, though the Jaz disks themselves looked different and used a different type of magnetic media. Jaz disks were like mini-hard drives that could hold Gigabytes of data as opposed to Zip disk's hundreds of Megabytes. The Jaz magnetic media itself resembled actual hard drive platters, whereas the magnetic media used with Zip disks were more like floppy disk media.

In 2018, I have a internal Zip drive installed in just about every vintage PC-AT compatible machine in my arsenal, and also on a modern machine. This makes a huge difference in convenience if you plan on working with vintage PC's. My PC-XT's use an external parallel port version. If you're inclined to install one of these bad boys in your retro battlestation, I can give you advice on how to get it going. If you're in the market to purchase one, I can tell you that chances are your device will work. Purchased maybe 10 of these from Ebay, every single one works just fine.

All in all, I give the tech 8/10. For what it was, Zip disks were handy as hell (for normies) at the time. At the very brief time. The data storage requirements doubled, tripled, quadrupled... in very short order.. and Zip technology just couldn't keep up with this demand for more and more capacity.
